Codes bound to a scale

Source: R/link.R
as_scale_unit.Rd

as_scale_unit() marks a vector of codes as belonging to one frame of one scale; it is what bind_scale() puts in a column. The result is a character vector of class scale_unit that carries the scale's name, its scale_id() and the frame. is_scale_unit() tests for it.

as_scale_unit(x, scale, frame)

is_scale_unit(x)

Arguments

x

A vector of codes; for is_scale_unit(), any object.

scale

The NestedScale the codes belong to.

frame

The frame the codes are at.

Value

as_scale_unit() a scale_unit vector as long as x; is_scale_unit() a single logical.

Details

Combining two such vectors (binding rows, joining) works when they are on the same scale and frame and is an error otherwise. Combined with a plain character vector the result stays bound, the plain codes being taken on trust; the verbs check codes against the scale when they use them.

See also

bind_scale(), scale_link()

Examples

s <- scale_example()
u <- as_scale_unit(c("P", "S", "P"), s, "sector")
u
#> <scale_unit<'example' [491e9cf6], sector>[3]>
#> [1] P S P
is_scale_unit(u)
#> [1] TRUE
as.character(u)
#> [1] "P" "S" "P"
